Definition: the hinder part; hence (adverb) behind, backward; also (as facing north) the West
BiblicalUsage: Achowr means behind, the backside, the hinder part. Abraham looked up and saw "behind him a ram caught in a thicket"; Moses "led the flock to the backside of the desert, and came to the mountain of God"; and David sang, "Thou hast beset me behind and before, and laid thine hand upon me." The word covers what is at our back — the provision we did not see, the place we did not expect, the God who surrounds us.
TheologicalSignificance: The word for 'behind' is a direction, not a teaching, and the comfort sits in the psalm it appears in, where God besets His people behind and before.
RelatedEvents: The Binding of Isaac; The Burning Bush
